gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now runs the new hvc_console survey beside the existing watchdog lanes so this missing tty anchor stops being invisible in the tranche review path.
A dedicated survey gate makes the missing hvc_console lane reviewable without overclaiming a Zig driver starter, tty registration path, or console-thread behavior that has not been ported.

The survey note records that the roadmap names hvc_console as a simple production driver anchor while the live Zigux tree still has no drivers/tty/hvc scaffold, keeping the gap explicit for later Phase 11 work.

The next honest bounded step is a tiny in-memory descriptor and console-slot bookkeeping starter around early vterm range checks, CRLF console write framing, and adapter-presence gating before any tty registration, kthread polling, or live hypervisor I/O.

Dedicated driver tests remain blocked until a first drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_console.zig scaffold exists to model console-slot validation, newline framing, and flush retry bookkeeping without touching tty core integration.

TTY driver registration, port lifetime, close-wait handling, sysrq integration, polling kthread behavior, and teardown parity should stay blocked until the lane first lands a bounded starter plus a hardware-validation matrix for those side effects.
